oviedo.s: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain. Founded around 761 under Fruela I, it was made the permanent royal seat by Alfonso II the Chaste in the early 9th century and remained the capital of the Kingdom of Asturias until the court moved to León in the early 10th…

oswald-of-northumbria.s: Oswald was king of Northumbria from 634 to 642. A son of Æthelfrith of Bernicia, he spent his youth in exile among the Gaels of Dál Riata and became a Christian on Iona.

o-raghallaigh.s: The Ó Raghallaigh, or O'Reillys, were a Gaelic Irish dynasty of the Uí Briúin Bréifne who ruled East Breifne, roughly modern County Cavan, from the 13th to the late 16th century. They gained power after the kingdom of Breifne split in 1256, ruled from Cavan town and the castle…

o-ruairc.s: The Ó Ruairc, or O'Rourkes, were a Gaelic Irish dynasty of the Uí Briúin Bréifne who ruled Breifne from the 10th century and, after the kingdom split in 1256, West Breifne, roughly modern County Leitrim, until the late 16th century. Several held the kingship of Connacht in the…

order-of-calatrava.s: The Order of Calatrava was a Castilian military order founded in 1158 to defend the fortress of Calatrava on the Guadiana against the Almohads after the Templars gave it up. Affiliated with the Cistercians, its knight-monks held large estates in La Mancha and fought in the…

orastie-mountains.s: The Orăștie Mountains are a range of the Southern Carpathians in Hunedoara County, Romania, south of the town of Orăștie. They were the heart of the Dacian kingdom from the 1st century BCE to 106 CE, with a ring of fortresses, among them Costești, Blidaru and Piatra Roșie,…

oethelwald-of-deira.s: Œthelwald of Deira was king of Deira from about 651 to 655, a son of Oswald of Northumbria, appointed under his uncle Oswiu. He sided with Penda of Mercia against Oswiu but held back his forces at the Battle of the Winwaed in 655, after which he disappears from the record.

osullivan-dynasty.s: The O'Sullivans (Ó Súilleabháin) were a Gaelic Irish family of the Eóganachta of Munster who, after the Anglo-Norman invasion, settled in south Kerry and west Cork. Their two main branches, O'Sullivan Mór and O'Sullivan Beare, were lords under the MacCarthy kings of Desmond.

ocarrolls-of-ely.s: The O'Carrolls (Ua Cerbaill) of Ely were the ruling dynasty of Éile in the Irish midlands from the 11th century, giving their name to the territory of Ely O'Carroll. They held strongholds such as Leap Castle and Birr and recovered lands taken by the Anglo-Normans.

olympias.s: Olympias was a Molossian princess of Epirus, daughter of King Neoptolemus I, who married Philip II of Macedon and was the mother of Alexander the Great. After Alexander's death she fought for her grandson Alexander IV in the wars of the Successors and had Philip III and his…

owain-gwynedd.s: Owain Gwynedd, son of Gruffudd ap Cynan, ruled Gwynedd from 1137 and made it the leading Welsh power. He pushed its frontier east towards the Dee, submitted to Henry II after the campaign of 1157, and in 1165 led a Welsh alliance against Henry's great invasion, which failed in…

obuda.s: Óbuda is the oldest part of Budapest, on the west bank of the Danube north of Buda. It stands on the site of Aquincum, capital of the Roman province of Pannonia Inferior, whose ruins survive there.

omri.s: Omri was king of Israel from about 884 to 873 BCE and founder of a dynasty that included his son Ahab. A general who won the throne in a civil war, he built a new capital at Samaria and made Israel a regional power, subduing Moab, as the Mesha Stele records.

old-uyghur-language.s: Old Uyghur was the Turkic language of the Uyghur Kingdom of Qocho and the Gansu Uyghurs from the 9th to the 14th centuries. Written mainly in the Old Uyghur script, derived from Sogdian, it was the language of a large Buddhist, Manichaean and Christian literature, much of it…

oba-of-lagos.s: The Oba of Lagos is the traditional ruler of Lagos, Nigeria. The line traces its origin to Ashipa, a war chief recognised by the Oba of Benin around the 16th century, and the early Obas of Lagos paid tribute to Benin.

obrien-dynasty.s: The O'Brien dynasty, in Irish Uí Briain, was a royal family of Munster descended from Brian Boru of the Dál gCais. From the 11th century they ruled as kings of Munster and later of Thomond, with Limerick as their chief seat, and Muirchertach Ua Briain claimed the high kingship…

omore.s: The O'Mores, Irish Ó Mórdha, were the ruling family of the Loígis in the Irish midlands from the 11th century, taking their name from an ancestor called Mórda. They recovered much of their territory from the Anglo-Normans in the 14th century and resisted the plantation of…

oun-kham.s: Oun Kham was king of Luang Prabang in the late 19th century, a vassal of Siam. In 1887 Chinese Haw bandits and their Tai allies sacked his capital, and the French vice-consul Auguste Pavie helped the elderly king escape down the Mekong.

ofu.s: Ofu is a small volcanic island in the Manuʻa group of American Samoa, separated from neighbouring Olosega by a narrow channel now crossed by a bridge. Its south coast has coral reefs and a beach that form part of the National Park of American Samoa.

olosega.s: Olosega is a small volcanic island in the Manuʻa group of American Samoa, linked to neighbouring Ofu by a bridge across a narrow channel. It has steep cliffs, and its small population lives in villages along the coast.

offas-dyke.s: Offa's Dyke is a linear earthwork running roughly along the border between England and Wales, generally attributed to Offa, king of Mercia from 757 to 796. Built as a bank with a ditch on its western side, it survives over about 130 kilometres and faced Welsh kingdoms such as…

olite.s: Olite is a town in Navarre, Spain, south of Pamplona. In the 15th century it was a favourite residence of the kings of Navarre, and Charles III the Noble built its large Gothic royal palace with towers, gardens and galleries.

olukonda.s: Olukonda is a village in Ondonga in northern Namibia and the site of the first Finnish Lutheran mission station among the Ovambo, founded in 1871. The missionary Martti Rautanen lived and worked there for decades.

ovambo-people.s: The Ovambo, or Aawambo, are a Bantu-speaking people of northern Namibia and southern Angola, the largest ethnic group of Namibia. They lived in a number of kingdoms, such as Ondonga and Kwanyama, on the floodplains around the Kunene and the Cuvelai, farming millet and keeping…

ovamboland.s: Ovamboland is the region of northern Namibia inhabited by the Ovambo people, between the Etosha Pan and the Angolan border. German rule hardly reached it, but after 1915 it came under South African administration and was later made an apartheid-era homeland with its own…

ofala-festival.s: The Ofala festival is an annual royal festival held by the Obi of Onitsha and by other traditional rulers in Igboland, especially in Anambra State, Nigeria. During the festival the king emerges from seclusion in full regalia to receive the homage of his chiefs, the Ndichie,…

olowo.s: The Olowo is the title of the king of Owo, a Yoruba kingdom in Ondo State, Nigeria. The royal line traces its descent to Ojugbelu, said to be a son or grandson of Oduduwa of Ile-Ife.

oswiu.s: Oswiu was king of Bernicia from 642 and of all Northumbria from 654 until his death in 670. In 655 he defeated and killed Penda of Mercia at the Battle of the Winwaed, briefly becoming overlord of much of England.

osijek.s: Osijek is the largest city of the Slavonia region in eastern Croatia, on the Drava river near its confluence with the Danube. Successor to the Roman town of Mursa, it was held by the Ottomans from 1526 to 1687, after which the Habsburgs built the star-shaped fortress of Tvrđa.

orbelian-dynasty.s: The Orbelians were an Armenian princely family who ruled much of Syunik and Vayots Dzor from the 13th to the 15th century. Branch of a family that had served the Georgian crown, they settled in Syunik under the Zakarid princes and later served the Mongols.

odyssey.s: The Odyssey is an ancient Greek epic poem attributed to Homer, probably composed in the late 8th or 7th century BCE. Its 24 books tell of the ten-year journey home of Odysseus, king of Ithaca, after the Trojan War, and of his revenge on the suitors of his wife Penelope.

ouedraogo.s: Ouedraogo is the legendary founder of the Mossi people of present-day Burkina Faso. Tradition tells that he was the son of Yennenga, a warrior princess of Mamprugu who rode north on a stallion, and of a hunter named Riale.

ofarrell.s: The O'Farrells were an Irish ruling family who held the lordship of Annaly, in what became County Longford, from the 12th century. Descended from the Uí Fergail of Tethba, they divided into rival branches but kept much of their independence until the Tudor reorganisation of…

ostergotland.s: Östergötland is a historical province in south-eastern Sweden, east of Lake Vättern, with Linköping and Norrköping as its main towns. One of the heartlands of the Geats, it holds the Rök runestone and Vadstena Abbey, founded by Saint Bridget.

ostrogoths.s: The Ostrogoths were the eastern branch of the Goths, who lived north of the Black Sea and came under Hunnic rule in the late 4th century. After the Huns' collapse they settled in Pannonia as Roman federates, and in 488 Theodoric the Great led them into Italy, where they…

oshere.s: Oshere was king of the Hwicce in the later 7th century, ruling under the overlordship of Mercia. He is known mainly from charters granting land to found minsters, part of the early church organisation of the Hwicce after the creation of the see of Worcester.

oshki.s: Oshki is a medieval Georgian monastery in the historic region of Tao, today in Erzurum Province, north-eastern Turkey. Its great domed church was built between 963 and 973 under David III Kuropalates and his brother Bagrat, and its walls carry long building inscriptions and…

oran.s: Oran is a port city on the north-western coast of Algeria, founded in 902 by Andalusi sailors. It was a trading port of the Zayyanids of Tlemcen, Spanish from 1509 to 1708 and again from 1732 to 1792, and then the seat of the Ottoman bey of the west.

ouarsenis.s: The Ouarsenis is a mountain range of the Tell Atlas in north-western Algeria, south of the Chelif valley, rising to almost 2,000 metres. After Roman and Vandal authority faded in the late 5th century it was the core of a Berber kingdom, and its rugged country later sheltered…

o-cleirigh.s: The Ó Cléirigh, or O'Clerys, were a learned family of historians and poets in the service of the O'Donnell lords of Tír Chonaill. Lughaidh Ó Cléirigh wrote a life of Red Hugh O'Donnell, and the friar Mícheál Ó Cléirigh led the compilation of the Annals of the Four Masters in…

odonnell-dynasty.s: The O'Donnells, Ó Domhnaill, were a branch of the Cenél Conaill who ruled Tír Chonaill in north-western Ireland from the 13th century to 1607. Based at Donegal Castle from 1474, they kept a strong fleet and Scottish mercenaries.

ocahan-dynasty.s: The O'Cahans, Ó Catháin, were a Gaelic ruling family in the north of present-day County Londonderry, Ireland, from the 12th century to the early 17th. As chief vassals of the O'Neills they took part in their inauguration at Tullyhogue.

oconnor-faly.s: The O'Connors Faly, Ua Conchobair Failge, were the ruling family of Uí Failge in the Irish midlands from the 11th century to the 1550s. They held out against the Anglo-Normans, raided the Pale and took black rent from its settlers.

o-ceallaigh.s: The Ó Ceallaigh, or O'Kellys, were the ruling family of Uí Maine in east Galway and south Roscommon from the 10th century to the 16th. They served the kings of Connacht in war, and Tadhg Mór Ua Cellaig fell at Clontarf in 1014.

omo-river.s: The Omo is a river of south-western Ethiopia that rises in the highlands west of Addis Ababa and flows south for about 760 kilometres into Lake Turkana. Its valley was bordered by kingdoms such as Janjero, Dawro, Kaffa and Wolaita.

ouahigouya.s: Ouahigouya is a city in northern Burkina Faso and the capital of the North Region. It was founded around 1780 by King Naaba Kango as the capital of the Mossi kingdom of Yatenga, and its ruler, the Yatenga Naaba, still resides there.

olaf-guthfrithson.s: Olaf Guthfrithson was a Viking king of Dublin from 934 and of York from 939 until his death in 941. In 937 he led the Dublin Norse in alliance with the Scots and the Britons of Strathclyde against King Æthelstan of England, and was defeated at the Battle of Brunanburh.

osh.s: Osh is the second largest city of Kyrgyzstan, on the eastern edge of the Fergana Valley. One of the oldest cities of Central Asia, it lay on the Silk Road, and its Sulaiman-Too mountain has been a place of pilgrimage for centuries and is now a World Heritage Site.

october-revolution.s: The October Revolution was the seizure of power in Petrograd by the Bolshevik Party under Vladimir Lenin on 25 October 1917 by the old Russian calendar, 7 November by the modern one. Red Guards and soldiers directed by the Military Revolutionary Committee overthrew the…

ogasawara-clan.s: The Ogasawara clan was a Japanese samurai family descended from the Seiwa Genji, taking its name from its estate in Kai province and later holding Shinano province. It became known for its school of etiquette and mounted archery.

odano-naotake.s: Odano Naotake was a samurai painter of the Kubota domain in Akita and the leading artist of the Akita school, which combined Japanese subjects with Western perspective and shading. Taught by Hiraga Gennai from 1773, he went to Edo and drew the illustrations for Kaitai Shinsho…

oesho.s: Oesho is a deity who appears on the coins of the Kushan Empire from the reign of Vima Kadphises, shown with several arms, a trident and often the bull Nandi. Most scholars identify him with the Indian god Shiva, though his name probably derives from that of the Iranian wind…

oghurs.s: The Oghurs were a group of Turkic-speaking peoples, including the Onogurs, Saragurs and Ogurs, who moved from Central Asia onto the Pontic–Caspian steppe around 463, according to the Byzantine historian Priscus. Their languages formed the Oghuric branch of Turkic, ancestral to…

ondjiva.s: Ondjiva is the capital of Cunene Province in southern Angola, near the Namibian border. It stands in the former heartland of the Kwanyama kingdom, the most populous of the Ovambo kingdoms, and in the colonial era was named Vila Pereira de Eça.

ottoneum.s: The Ottoneum is a building in Kassel, Germany, built from 1604 to 1606 for Landgrave Maurice of Hesse-Kassel and named after his son Otto. It was the first permanent theatre building in Germany, used by the court's company of actors.

odawara.s: Odawara is a city in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, on Sagami Bay at the eastern foot of the Hakone mountains. From the late 15th century Odawara Castle was the seat of the Later Hojo clan, who made it one of the largest castle towns in eastern Japan until Toyotomi Hideyoshi…

olous.s: Olous was an ancient Greek city on the Gulf of Mirabello in eastern Crete, near modern Elounda. Its remains now lie partly under the sea because of the sinking of the coast.

oskars-dankers.s: Oskars Dankers was a Latvian general who headed the Latvian Self-Administration, the local administration under German occupation, from 1942 to 1945. A former officer of the Russian Imperial Army, he became a general in the army of independent Latvia between the wars.

octavians-illyrian-campaign.s: Octavian's Illyrian campaign of 35–33 BCE was a series of Roman operations led by the future Augustus along the eastern Adriatic and in its hinterland. He subdued the Iapydes, was wounded at the siege of their stronghold Metulum, took the Pannonian town of Siscia and defeated…

oath-of-pontida.s: The Oath of Pontida is the traditional founding act of the Lombard League, said to have been sworn on 7 April 1167 at the abbey of Pontida near Bergamo by representatives of Milan, Cremona, Bergamo, Brescia, Mantua and other cities. They pledged mutual aid against the emperor…

ommelanden.s: The Ommelanden are the rural Frisian districts surrounding the city of Groningen in the northern Netherlands. In the Middle Ages they were self-governing farming communities that the city sought to dominate through its staple rights and courts.

ostringen.s: Östringen was one of the medieval Frisian lands of north-western Germany, lying around the town of Jever west of the Jade bay. Like its neighbours it was a self-governing peasant community within the Frisian freedom until local chieftains rose to power in the 14th century.

obersontheim.s: Obersontheim is a village in the district of Schwäbisch Hall in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. In the early modern period it was the residence of the Limpurg-Sontheim branch of the Schenks of Limpurg, whose castle survives.

ottone-visconti.s: Ottone Visconti was Archbishop of Milan from 1262 and the founder of Visconti power in the city. Long kept out of Milan by the ruling della Torre family, he defeated them at the Battle of Desio in 1277 and took control of the city.

oenotrians.s: The Oenotrians were an ancient Italic people of southern Italy, recorded by Greek writers as living in what are now Basilicata and Calabria before the founding of the Greek colonies in the 8th century BCE. The Greeks called the region Oenotria, and the name Italia first…

otho.s: Otho (Marcus Salvius Otho) was Roman emperor for three months in 69 CE, the Year of the Four Emperors. A friend of Nero, he was sent to govern Lusitania in 58 after Nero took his wife Poppaea Sabina, and ruled the province for ten years.

olympos-lycia.s: Olympos was a city on the coast of eastern Lycia, south-west of modern Antalya in Turkey, and one of the six leading members of the Lycian League. In the early 1st century BCE it was a base of the pirate chief Zeniketes, who burned himself in his house when Publius Servilius…

omalley-clan.s: The O'Malleys (Ó Máille) were a Gaelic seafaring lineage of Umall, around Clew Bay in County Mayo, western Ireland. Unusual among Irish lords for their fleets, they fished, traded and raided along the Atlantic coast and paid dues to the Mac William Burkes.

oujda.s: Oujda is a city in north-eastern Morocco, near the border with Algeria. It was founded in 994 by Ziri ibn Atiyya, chief of the Maghrawa Berbers, and changed hands repeatedly between the rulers of Morocco and those of Tlemcen and later Ottoman Algeria.

onilahy-river.s: The Onilahy is a river of south-western Madagascar, which flows west across the dry plateau and reaches the Mozambique Channel at St Augustine's Bay, south of Toliara. Its valley bordered the lands of the Mahafaly kingdoms to the south.

omdurman.s: Omdurman is a city on the west bank of the Nile opposite Khartoum, part of Sudan's largest urban area. The Mahdi made it his base during the siege of Khartoum, and his successor the Khalifa Abdallahi made it the capital of the Mahdist State, where the Mahdi's tomb was built.

old-dongola.s: Old Dongola, known in Nubian as Tungul, is an abandoned town on the east bank of the Nile in northern Sudan, the capital of the Christian kingdom of Makuria from about the 6th to the 14th century. Its ruins include churches, palaces and the royal throne hall, which was…

onn-jaafar.s: Onn Jaafar was a Malay politician and chief minister of Johor who led the opposition to the Malayan Union and founded the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) in 1946. He left UMNO in 1951 after failing to open it to non-Malays and founded the Independence of Malaya…

oslo-accords.s: The Oslo Accords were the agreements of 1993 and 1995 between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization, negotiated secretly in Norway, in which each side recognised the other for the first time. They created a Palestinian Authority with limited self-government in parts…

otakars.s: The Otakars were a noble dynasty, counts of Steyr in Upper Austria, who ruled the Carantanian March from 1056. They made it independent of Carinthia, and the land took its name, Styria, from their castle of Steyr.

odysseus.s: Odysseus, called Ulysses by the Romans, is the legendary king of Ithaca in Greek myth, a hero of the Trojan War famous for his cunning, credited with the stratagem of the wooden horse. Homer's Odyssey tells of his ten-year voyage home, including his escape from the Cyclops…

oezalces.s: Oezalces was king of the Massylii in Numidia around 207–206 BCE. The brother of King Gaia, he succeeded him under the Numidian custom by which the eldest male of the royal family inherited, but died soon afterwards.

oria-apulia.s: Oria is a hill town in the province of Brindisi in Apulia, southern Italy. As ancient Uria it was one of the main centres of the Messapians, and Herodotus reports a tradition that it was founded by Cretans.

otomi.s: The Otomi are an indigenous people of central Mexico, living mainly in the states of Hidalgo, México and Querétaro and speaking Otomian languages of the Oto-Manguean family. Before the Spanish conquest they lived both inside the Aztec Empire and in independent lordships such…

oka-crisis.s: The Oka crisis was a 78-day armed stand-off in 1990 between Mohawk protesters and the Quebec police and Canadian army near the town of Oka, west of Montreal. It began when Mohawks of Kanesatake blocked a road to stop a golf course from being extended onto disputed land,…

oka-river.s: The Oka is a river of European Russia, about 1,500 kilometres long, the largest right-bank tributary of the Volga, which it joins at Nizhny Novgorod. Rising south of Oryol, it flows past Kaluga, Serpukhov, Ryazan and Murom.

oyu-tolgoi.s: Oyu Tolgoi is a copper and gold mine in the South Gobi desert of Mongolia, one of the largest such deposits in the world. Discovered in 2001, it is developed by a company jointly owned by the Mongolian government and Rio Tinto, with open-pit production beginning in 2013 and a…

okmulgee.s: Okmulgee is a town in eastern Oklahoma in the United States. It became the capital of the Muscogee Nation in 1867, after its removal from the South-East, and its sandstone Creek Council House of 1878 now serves as a museum.

oedipus.s: In Greek mythology, Oedipus was a king of Thebes who unknowingly killed his father Laius and married his mother Jocasta, fulfilling a prophecy. On discovering the truth he blinded himself and went into exile.

okinawa-island.s: Okinawa Island is the largest island of the Ryukyu chain, between Kyushu and Taiwan, and the site of Naha, capital of Okinawa Prefecture. In the 14th century it was divided among the three kingdoms of Hokuzan, Chuzan and Nanzan, united in 1429 as the Ryukyu Kingdom with its…

operation-car-wash.s: Operation Car Wash, or Lava Jato, was a Brazilian criminal investigation launched in 2014 that uncovered a vast system of bribes paid by construction firms to executives of the state oil company Petrobras and to politicians. It led to the conviction of many businessmen and…

ollovico.s: Ollovico was a king of the Nitiobroges, a Gaulish people on the Garonne, in the 1st century BCE. Julius Caesar records in his Gallic War that he had been honoured by the Roman Senate with the title of 'friend'.

oda-nobutada.s: Oda Nobutada was the eldest son and heir of the Japanese warlord Oda Nobunaga. He received headship of the Oda clan in the mid-1570s and led the campaign that destroyed the Takeda in 1582.

okubo-tadachika.s: Ōkubo Tadachika was a Japanese daimyo and senior retainer of Tokugawa Ieyasu, lord of the Odawara Domain in Sagami Province and a leading official of the early Tokugawa shogunate. In 1614 he was stripped of his domain and exiled to Ōmi Province, probably as a result of rivalry…

odrysians.s: The Odrysians were a Thracian people of the Hebrus (Maritsa) valley in what is now southern Bulgaria and European Turkey. Under Teres I in the 5th century BCE they united many Thracian tribes in the Odrysian kingdom, the most powerful state in Thrace, which drew tribute from…

okayama.s: Okayama is a city in western Honshu, Japan, and the capital of Okayama Prefecture, near the Inland Sea coast. It grew around Okayama Castle, completed by Ukita Hideie in the late 16th century, and from 1632 was the seat of the Ikeda daimyo of the Okayama Domain.

okayama-prefecture.s: Okayama Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan in the Chūgoku region of western Honshu, facing the Inland Sea, with its capital at Okayama. It was created after the abolition of the domains in 1871 and covers the old provinces of Bizen, Bitchū and Mimasaka.

obong-of-calabar.s: The Obong of Calabar is the title of the paramount traditional ruler of the Efik people of Calabar in south-eastern Nigeria. The office grew in the 19th and early 20th centuries out of the leadership of the Efik trading towns that Europeans called Old Calabar.

olynthiacs.s: The Olynthiacs are three political speeches delivered by the Athenian orator Demosthenes in 349–348 BCE. They urged Athens to send effective help to Olynthus, the leading city of the Chalcidian League, which was under attack by Philip II of Macedon.

oneida-lake.s: Oneida Lake is the largest lake lying wholly within New York State, north-east of Syracuse. Its shores and the creeks flowing into it were the homeland of the Oneida nation of the Iroquois Confederacy, and it lay on the water route linking the Mohawk River to Lake Ontario.

onogurs.s: The Onogurs were a Turkic-speaking nomadic people of the Pontic–Caspian steppe, first recorded in 463 CE when they sent envoys to Constantinople. Their name is usually interpreted as 'ten Oghurs', meaning ten tribes.

orangia-unie.s: Orangia Unie was a political party of the Orange River Colony formed by Afrikaner leaders after the Second Boer War, among them Abraham Fischer, J. B. M. Hertzog and Christiaan de Wet. It won the first election under responsible government in 1907, and Fischer became prime…

oorlam.s: The Oorlam were groups of Khoekhoe and mixed descent from the Cape Colony frontier who had adopted horses, firearms, Cape Dutch speech and Christianity. From the late 18th century bands such as the Afrikaners and the Witboois migrated north across the Orange River into…

otjimbingwe.s: Otjimbingwe is a settlement on the Swakop River in central Namibia, west of Windhoek. A Rhenish mission station was founded there in 1849, and it became a trading and copper-mining centre on the route to Walvis Bay.

ogooue.s: The Ogooué is the main river of Gabon, flowing about 1,200 kilometres from the Republic of the Congo to the Atlantic, where it forms a wide delta near Cape Lopez and Port-Gentil. Its basin covers most of the country.

otomo-sorin.s: Ōtomo Sōrin, born Ōtomo Yoshishige, was a daimyo of Bungo in Kyushu who led his clan from 1550. He welcomed Francis Xavier in 1551, traded with the Portuguese and was baptised in 1578, becoming one of the best-known Christian lords of Japan.

otomo-yoshimune.s: Ōtomo Yoshimune was the son of Ōtomo Sōrin and the last daimyo of the Ōtomo clan in Bungo. Hard pressed by the Shimazu in the 1580s, he was saved by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Kyushu, but in 1593 Hideyoshi stripped him of his lands for abandoning his post during the…

ouchi-clan.s: The Ōuchi were a samurai clan of western Japan, based in Suō Province, who claimed descent from a prince of the Korean kingdom of Baekje. As military governors they built a powerful domain around Yamaguchi, dominated trade with Ming China and Korea, and patronised learning and…

oeantheia.s: Oeantheia was an ancient Greek town of Ozolian Locris on the northern shore of the Gulf of Corinth, usually identified with modern Galaxidi. With neighbouring Chaleion it concluded a 5th-century BCE agreement, inscribed on a bronze tablet, regulating reprisals and the rights…

order-of-battle-against-the-alans.n: Order of Battle against the Alans
order-of-battle-against-the-alans.s: The Order of Battle against the Alans is a short Greek military treatise by Arrian, governor of Cappadocia, written around 135 CE when an Alan invasion threatened the province. It describes how he would march and deploy his legions and auxiliaries, with infantry in a deep…

ordino.s: Ordino is one of the seven parishes of Andorra and the name of its main village, in the north of the principality on the Valira del Nord. Long a centre of iron working and of wealthy landowning families, it preserves the Casa d'Areny-Plandolit, home of the family of Guillem…

oscar-ribas-reig.s: Òscar Ribas Reig was an Andorran politician who became the first head of government of Andorra in 1982, after the reforms of 1981 created an executive council. He served from 1982 to 1984 and again from 1990 to 1994, leading the country through the adoption of its first…

oghuz-khan.s: Oghuz Khan is the legendary ancestor of the Oghuz Turks, celebrated in Turkic epic and genealogical tradition. Stories of his conquests and of his twenty-four grandsons, the ancestors of the Oghuz tribes, are told in the Uyghur Oghuzname and in Rashid al-Din's history.

ostracism.s: Ostracism was an Athenian procedure by which the Assembly could exile a leading citizen for ten years without loss of property, by writing his name on potsherds, ostraka. First used in 487 BCE, possibly introduced in the reforms of Cleisthenes, it removed figures such as…

october-diploma.s: The October Diploma was a constitutional decree issued by Emperor Franz Joseph I on 20 October 1860, after defeat in Italy had discredited neo-absolutism. It restored the provincial diets and created an imperial council with a federalist, aristocratic bent, but it satisfied…

organisation-todt.s: Organisation Todt was the civil and military engineering organisation of Nazi Germany, named after its founder Fritz Todt and later run by Albert Speer. It built the Westwall, the Atlantic Wall and other fortifications, roads and military works across occupied Europe, relying…

onchestus.s: Onchestus was an ancient site in Boeotia between Lake Copais and Thebes, best known for its sanctuary of Poseidon, mentioned in Homer's Catalogue of Ships and the Homeric Hymn to Apollo. The sanctuary was a shared religious centre of the Boeotians, and in the Hellenistic…

omar-ali-saifuddien-iii.s: Omar Ali Saifuddien III was the 28th sultan of Brunei, reigning from 1950 to 1967. Using growing oil revenue, he funded schools, hospitals and roads, and he granted the 1959 constitution that gave Brunei internal self-government.

omar-ali-saifuddien-mosque.s: The Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque is a royal mosque in Bandar Seri Begawan, the capital of Brunei, completed in 1958 and named after Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien III. Standing beside an artificial lagoon near the water village of Kampong Ayer, it has a golden dome and a tall…

omar-ali-saifuddin-ii.s: Omar Ali Saifuddin II was sultan of Brunei from 1828 to 1852. During his reign the English adventurer James Brooke was granted Sarawak and became its rajah in 1841, beginning the loss of Brunei's territories, and in 1846 the island of Labuan was ceded to Britain after a…

oeconomica.s: The Oeconomica is a Greek treatise on household and state finance attributed to Aristotle but written by members of his school. Its second book collects examples of the expedients by which cities and rulers raised money in emergencies, including Byzantium, which sold public…

ordinance-50.s: Ordinance 50 was a law of the Cape Colony issued in 1828 that freed the Khoikhoi and other free people of colour from the pass laws and forced labour contracts imposed on them, and gave them equal legal standing with white colonists. It was promoted by the missionary John…

oenopides.s: Oenopides of Chios was a Greek astronomer and mathematician of the fifth century BCE. He is credited with discovering the obliquity of the ecliptic, the tilt of the sun's annual path against the celestial equator, and with proposing a 'Great Year' of 59 years to reconcile…

orchies.s: Orchies is a small town in the Nord department of northern France, between Lille and Douai. With Lille and Douai it formed Walloon Flanders, the French-speaking south of the County of Flanders, and was transferred with them to the French crown in 1312 after the Franco-Flemish…

otto-iv-holy-roman-emperor.s: Otto IV, of the Welf dynasty, was king of Germany from 1198 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1209. A son of Henry the Lion and nephew of Richard I of England, he fought the Staufer Philip of Swabia for the crown and later broke with Pope Innocent III.

oslo.s: Oslo is the capital of Norway, at the head of the Oslofjord. Founded in the 11th century, it became the royal capital around 1300.

ole-romer.s: Ole Rømer was a Danish astronomer who in 1676, working at the Paris Observatory, showed from the timing of eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io that light travels at a finite speed and made the first estimate of it. Back in Copenhagen he was royal mathematician and chief of police,…

odilo-of-bavaria.s: Odilo was an Agilolfing duke of Bavaria from about 736 until his death in 748. With Saint Boniface he organised the Bavarian church into the dioceses of Salzburg, Regensburg, Freising and Passau in 739.

orlande-de-lassus.s: Orlande de Lassus was a Franco-Flemish composer, born in Mons in Hainaut around 1532, and one of the most prolific and celebrated musicians of the late Renaissance. From 1556 he served the Wittelsbach court of Albert V in Munich, leading its chapel from 1563 until his death in…

otto-i-duke-of-bavaria.s: Otto I of Wittelsbach was a Bavarian count palatine and a loyal follower of Frederick Barbarossa, whom he served on campaigns in Italy. When Barbarossa deposed Henry the Lion in 1180, he gave the reduced Duchy of Bavaria to Otto, founding the rule of the House of Wittelsbach,…

old-university-of-leuven.s: The Old University of Leuven was founded in 1425 by Pope Martin V at the request of Duke John IV of Brabant and became one of the great universities of Catholic Europe. Erasmus worked there, the Collegium Trilingue made it a centre of humanism, and in the Counter-Reformation…

olivier-de-clisson.s: Olivier de Clisson was a Breton soldier who fought first for John of Montfort, losing an eye at Auray in 1364, and then for France. He succeeded Bertrand du Guesclin as constable of France in 1380 and commanded at the French victory over the Flemish at Roosebeke in 1382.

odo-iii-duke-of-burgundy.s: Odo III was duke of Burgundy from 1192 to 1218, the son of Hugh III. A loyal ally of Philip II of France, he fought at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214 and took part in the Albigensian Crusade.

odo-iv-duke-of-burgundy.s: Odo IV was duke of Burgundy from 1315 to 1349. His marriage in 1318 to Joan, daughter of Philip V of France, brought him the Free County of Burgundy and Artois, which she inherited in 1330, uniting the two Burgundies.

on-crimes-and-punishments.s: On Crimes and Punishments is a treatise by Cesare Beccaria, published anonymously in Livorno in 1764. It argued that punishments should be proportionate, prompt and certain, and condemned torture and capital punishment as cruel and useless.

ospedale-maggiore-milan.s: The Ospedale Maggiore, known as the Ca' Granda, is a hospital building in Milan founded in 1456 by Francesco Sforza and Bianca Maria Visconti to bring together the city's many small hospitals. Designed by Filarete around a grid of courtyards, it was one of the first large…

orderic-vitalis.s: Orderic Vitalis was an English-born monk of the Norman abbey of Saint-Évroul, sent there from Shropshire as a boy of ten. His Ecclesiastical History, written between about 1114 and 1141, is the most important narrative of Anglo-Norman history for the late eleventh and early…

odoardo-farnese-duke-of-parma.s: Odoardo Farnese was duke of Parma and Piacenza from 1622. Seeking military glory, he allied with France against Spain in 1635, bringing a devastating Spanish invasion of the Piacenza countryside until he made peace in 1637.

ottavio-farnese.s: Ottavio Farnese was duke of Parma and Piacenza from 1547, a grandson of Pope Paul III. After his father Pier Luigi was murdered, he held on to Parma against imperial pressure, fighting the War of Parma with French support in 1551–1552.

order-of-saints-maurice-and-lazarus.n: Order of Saints Maurice and Lazarus
order-of-saints-maurice-and-lazarus.s: The Order of Saints Maurice and Lazarus is a dynastic order of chivalry of the house of Savoy, created in 1572 when Pope Gregory XIII merged the Order of Saint Maurice with the Order of Saint Lazarus at the request of Duke Emmanuel Philibert. It became a leading order of the…

otto-the-illustrious.s: Otto the Illustrious was a Saxon count of the Liudolfing family who held a dominant position in Saxony and Thuringia from 880 until his death in 912. A son of Count Liudolf, he succeeded his brother Bruno, who was killed fighting the Vikings, and he is counted as Duke of Saxony.

oreste-baratieri.s: Oreste Baratieri (1841–1901) was an Italian general who had fought with Garibaldi's Thousand and became governor of the colony of Eritrea in the early 1890s. Commanding the Italian army in the First Italo-Ethiopian War, he was decisively defeated by Menelik II at the Battle of…

onglos.s: The Onglos was the area near the Danube delta, probably in southern Bessarabia or northern Dobruja, where the Bulgars of Asparuh settled in the 670s. Protected by rivers and marshes, it served as their base for crossing the Danube.

oper-am-gansemarkt.s: The Oper am Gänsemarkt was an opera house in Hamburg, opened in 1678 as the first public opera house in Germany. Composers such as Reinhard Keiser, the young George Frideric Handel and Georg Philipp Telemann wrote German-language operas for it, making it the centre of early…

operation-gomorrah.s: Operation Gomorrah was a series of British and American air raids on Hamburg in late July and early August 1943. On the night of 27–28 July, hot, dry weather and concentrated bombing created a firestorm that devastated eastern districts of the city.

ordeelbook.s: The Ordeelbook of 1270 is Hamburg's first written code of city law, compiled in Low German. It covers private, criminal and procedural law as practised in the city's courts.

operation-torch.s: Operation Torch was the Allied invasion of French North Africa in November 1942, with landings around Casablanca, Oran and Algiers. American and British forces met brief resistance from Vichy French troops before Admiral Darlan agreed to a ceasefire.

osian.s: Osian is an ancient town in the Thar Desert near Jodhpur in Rajasthan, India, once an important trading centre on caravan routes. It is known for a group of Hindu and Jain temples built from the eighth to the twelfth century, among them the Mahavira temple, dated to the time…

oresund.s: The Øresund, or the Sound, is the strait between the Danish island of Zealand and Scania in southern Sweden, the main passage between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea. At its narrowest, between Helsingør and Helsingborg, it is about four kilometres wide.

old-kannada.s: Old Kannada, or Halegannada, is the form of the Kannada language used in inscriptions and literature of the later first and early second millennium CE, from the Rashtrakuta period to the Hoysalas. Its classical works include the Kavirajamarga of the 9th century and the poems…

osman-sagar.s: Osman Sagar, also called Gandipet, is a reservoir on the Musi river west of Hyderabad, completed in 1920 under the Nizam Osman Ali Khan, after whom it is named. Built after the Musi flood of 1908 killed thousands in the city, it controlled floods and long served as a main…

ollantaytambo.s: Ollantaytambo is a town and Inca archaeological site in the Sacred Valley of the Urubamba, north-west of Cusco in Peru. It was a royal estate of the Inca ruler Pachacuti, with temples, terraces and a fortress of fitted stone, and in 1537 Manco Inca defeated a Spanish attack…

operation-trikora.s: Operation Trikora was the Indonesian campaign of 1961–1962 to take western New Guinea from the Netherlands, named after the 'People's Triple Command' that Sukarno proclaimed in December 1961. Indonesian forces, under a command led by Suharto, landed paratroops and infiltrators…

otrar.s: Otrar was a medieval oasis city on the middle Syr Darya in southern Kazakhstan, an important town of the Silk Road. In 1218 its governor massacred a caravan of merchants sent by Genghis Khan, the incident that provoked the Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire; the city…

old-bavaria.s: Old Bavaria is the historic core of Bavaria, made up of Upper Bavaria, Lower Bavaria and the Upper Palatinate, as distinct from Franconia and Swabia, which were joined to the state in the Napoleonic era. A Catholic region of large peasant farms and Bavarian dialects, it was…

otto-v-margrave-of-brandenburg.s: Otto V, called the Long, was a margrave of Brandenburg of the Ascanian house. After Ottokar II of Bohemia was killed at the Battle on the Marchfeld in 1278, he became guardian of the young Wenceslaus II and governed Bohemia.

old-town-square-prague.s: Old Town Square is the main square of Prague's Old Town, a market place since the twelfth century. Around it stand the Old Town Hall with its astronomical clock, the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn and the Baroque Kinsky Palace.

order-of-santiago.s: The Order of Santiago was a military order founded around 1170 at Cáceres in the Kingdom of León and approved by the pope in 1175. Named after St James, patron of Spain, it soon made Uclés in Castile its main seat and became the largest and richest of the Spanish military…

ordinance-of-villers-cotterets.s: The Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts was a reforming law issued by Francis I of France in August 1539 at his château of Villers-Cotterêts. Among its many articles on justice and administration, it required that legal and official acts be written in French rather than Latin, and…

ottoman-hungary.s: Ottoman Hungary was the central and southern part of the medieval Kingdom of Hungary ruled by the Ottoman Empire from the capture of Buda in 1541 until the reconquest of the 1680s and 1690s. Organised mainly in the eyalets of Buda and Temesvár, it was a frontier zone of…

oliver-goldsmith.s: Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish writer, educated at Trinity College Dublin, who made his career in London as a member of Samuel Johnson's circle. He is remembered for the novel The Vicar of Wakefield (1766), the poem The Deserted Village (1770) and the comedy She Stoops to…

omride-dynasty.s: The Omride dynasty was the royal house of the Kingdom of Israel founded by Omri around 885 BCE and destroyed by Jehu's coup around 841 BCE. Under Omri and Ahab Israel became a significant regional power, building Samaria as its capital, allying with Phoenicia and Judah and…

ovra.s: The OVRA was the secret political police of Fascist Italy, organised from 1927 under the Ministry of the Interior while Arturo Bocchini was chief of police. It ran a large network of informers that watched and arrested opponents of the regime, many of whom were sent to…

otranto.s: Otranto is a town on the coast of Apulia, the easternmost town of Italy, facing Albania across the Strait of Otranto. An ancient Greek and Byzantine port, it was captured by an Ottoman force in August 1480, when many inhabitants were killed, including the 813 later venerated…

osberht-of-northumbria.s: Osberht (died 867) was king of Northumbria from about 849. In the 860s he was displaced by Ælla, but when the Great Heathen Army captured York in 866 the two rivals made peace to fight the Danes together.

osred-i-of-northumbria.s: Osred I (c. 697–716) became king of Northumbria as a boy of about eight on the death of his father Aldfrith in 705, after a disputed succession. His reign was later remembered for violence and the abuse of nuns, according to a letter of Saint Boniface.

oswulf-of-northumbria.s: Oswulf was king of Northumbria from 758 to 759, the son of King Eadberht, who abdicated in his favour to become a monk at York. Within a year, on 24 July 759, he was murdered by members of his own household.

olaf-ii-of-denmark.s: Olaf II of Denmark, also Olaf IV of Norway, was the son of Haakon VI of Norway and Margaret, daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark. Elected king of Denmark in 1376 as a child, he inherited Norway on his father's death in 1380, beginning the union of the two crowns that lasted…

olaf-iii-of-norway.s: Olaf III of Norway, known as Olaf Kyrre ('the Peaceful'), was the son of Harald Hardrada and survived his father's defeat at Stamford Bridge in 1066. King of Norway from 1067 to 1093, he kept the kingdom at peace, encouraged trade and the growth of towns, and is traditionally…

olav-engelbrektsson.s: Olav Engelbrektsson was the last Catholic archbishop of Nidaros (Trondheim), from 1523, and the leading figure of the Norwegian council of the realm. He opposed Christian III during the Count's Feud and tried to defend Norway's separate status and the old church, but when…

oscarsborg-fortress.s: Oscarsborg Fortress is a coastal fortress on islands in the Drøbak Sound of the Oslofjord, south of Oslo, built mainly in the mid-nineteenth century. On 9 April 1940 its old guns and torpedo battery sank the German heavy cruiser Blücher, which was carrying troops to occupy Oslo.

order-of-aviz.s: The Order of Aviz was a Portuguese military religious order founded in the twelfth century to fight the Moors, taking its name from its seat at Aviz in the Alentejo, granted in 1211. Following the Cistercian rule, it took part in the Reconquista of southern Portugal.

ordenacoes-afonsinas.s: The Ordenações Afonsinas were the first general code of Portuguese law, completed around 1446 in the reign of Afonso V, after whom they are named. In five books they gathered royal laws, customs and rules from Roman and canon law.

order-of-christ-portugal.s: The Order of Christ was a Portuguese military religious order founded by King Denis in 1319, with the approval of Pope John XXII, to take over the property of the suppressed Knights Templar. Based at Tomar from 1357, it was governed in the fifteenth century by Prince Henry the…

os-lusiadas.s: Os Lusíadas (The Lusiads) is the national epic of Portugal, written by Luís de Camões and published in Lisbon in 1572. In ten cantos of ottava rima it tells of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India in 1497–1499 and, through it, the history of the Portuguese people, mixing classical…

oswestry.s: Oswestry is a market town in Shropshire, England, close to the Welsh border. Its name is linked with King Oswald of Northumbria, killed nearby at the Battle of Maserfield in 642.

ordinance-of-alsno.s: The Ordinance of Alsnö was a decree issued around 1280 by King Magnus Ladulås of Sweden at Alsnö on Lake Mälaren. It freed from taxation those men who served the king as armoured horsemen, creating a privileged class of tax-exempt warriors that became the basis of the Swedish…

ordinatio-imperii.s: The Ordinatio imperii was a decree issued by the Frankish emperor Louis the Pious at Aachen in 817 to settle his succession. It made his eldest son Lothar co-emperor and heir to the undivided empire, while his younger sons Pippin and Louis received Aquitaine and Bavaria as…

orosius.s: Orosius, or Paulus Orosius, was a Christian priest and historian from Roman Hispania and a pupil of Augustine of Hippo. His Seven Books of History against the Pagans, written around 417, surveys world history to argue that disasters had been worse before Christianity.

order-of-alcantara.s: The Order of Alcántara is a Spanish military religious order founded in the 12th century in the Kingdom of León, originally as the Order of San Julián del Pereiro. It took its name from the town of Alcántara on the Tagus, entrusted to it in 1218, and fought in the Reconquista…

ossonoba.s: Ossonoba was a town of Roman Lusitania on the Algarve coast of southern Portugal, at or near the site of modern Faro. A port with fish-salting works, it became the seat of a bishop in late antiquity, and its bishop Ithacius was a leading accuser of Priscillian in the 380s.

oderbruch.s: The Oderbruch is a lowland on the west bank of the Oder in Brandenburg, Germany, along the Polish border. Once a marshy floodplain, it was drained on the orders of Frederick the Great from 1747 to 1753, when the Oder was given a new bed, and settled with colonists, creating…

ostrava.s: Ostrava is the third-largest city of the Czech Republic, on the Oder near the Polish border, where Moravia meets Czech Silesia. From the nineteenth century it grew into the centre of a major coalfield and of heavy industry around the Vítkovice ironworks.

octavio-paz.s: Octavio Paz was a Mexican poet, essayist and diplomat who received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1990. His essay The Labyrinth of Solitude (1950) is a classic study of Mexican identity, and his poetry includes Sunstone.

operation-1027.s: Operation 1027 was an offensive launched on 27 October 2023 by the Three Brotherhood Alliance of ethnic armed groups in northern Shan State, Myanmar. It captured towns, military posts and border crossings with China, including Laukkai, and was the military junta's greatest…

oberkommando-der-wehrmacht.s: The Oberkommando der Wehrmacht (OKW), or High Command of the Armed Forces, was created by Hitler in February 1938 when he abolished the war ministry and took personal command of the German armed forces. Headed by Wilhelm Keitel, with Alfred Jodl as chief of operations, it…

operation-bagration.s: Operation Bagration was the Soviet summer offensive of 1944 in Belarus, launched on 22–23 June. It destroyed most of the German Army Group Centre, one of the greatest defeats in German military history, and carried the Red Army to the Vistula and the borders of East Prussia by…

our-lady-of-guadalupe.s: Our Lady of Guadalupe is a title of the Virgin Mary associated with apparitions to Juan Diego at Tepeyac, near Mexico City, in December 1531, and with the image venerated in her basilica there. The devotion grew through the colonial period into a symbol shared by indigenous…

onfim.s: Onfim was a boy who lived in Novgorod in the thirteenth century, probably aged six or seven, known from a group of birchbark documents found by archaeologists in 1956. They contain his writing exercises, copied prayers and drawings of himself as a warrior on horseback slaying…

oreshek-fortress.s: Oreshek is a fortress on an island at the source of the Neva River from Lake Ladoga, founded by Novgorod in 1323. The Treaty of Nöteborg, the first border agreement between Novgorod and Sweden, was signed there the same year.

orange-river-colony.s: The Orange River Colony was the British colony formed from the annexed Orange Free State during the Second Boer War, proclaimed in May 1900 and confirmed by the Treaty of Vereeniging in 1902. It received responsible government in 1907 and in 1910 became the Orange Free State…

orange-free-state-province.s: The Orange Free State Province was one of the four provinces of the Union of South Africa and later the Republic of South Africa, formed in 1910 from the Orange River Colony, with Bloemfontein as its capital. It kept the borders of the former Boer republic, and in 1994 it…

otbert.s: Otbert was prince-bishop of Liège from 1091 to 1119 and a loyal supporter of Emperor Henry IV in the Investiture Controversy, sheltering him at Liège before his death in 1106. In 1096 he bought the castle and lordship of Bouillon from Godfrey of Bouillon, who needed money for…

ourthe.s: The Ourthe is a river in the Belgian Ardennes, about 165 kilometres long, which flows north to join the Meuse at Liège. From 1795 to 1814 it gave its name to the French department of the Ourthe, centred on Liège.

occitania.s: Occitania is the historical region of southern France, with parts of Italy and Spain, where the Occitan language was spoken. In the twelfth and early thirteenth centuries the counts of Barcelona and kings of Aragon held lands and influence there, which ended with the…

outer-mongolia.s: Outer Mongolia was the northern part of Mongolia under the Qing dynasty, inhabited mainly by the Khalkha Mongols, who submitted to the Kangxi Emperor in 1691. After the fall of the Qing it declared independence in 1911 under the Bogd Khan, and with Soviet support became the…

oecd.s: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) is an intergovernmental organisation of mostly high-income democracies, founded in 1961 as the successor to the body that administered Marshall Plan aid. Based in Paris, it gathers economic statistics, compares…

oriente-ecuador.s: The Oriente is the Amazonian lowland of eastern Ecuador, east of the Andes, covering nearly half the country's territory but home to a small share of its population, including many indigenous peoples. Much of the larger Amazon territory once claimed by Ecuador was lost to Peru…

oswaldo-guayasamin.s: Oswaldo Guayasamín was an Ecuadorian painter and sculptor of indigenous and mestizo descent. His expressionist works, such as the series Huacayñán and The Age of Wrath, depicted suffering, oppression and violence in Latin America and the wider world.

oscar-romero.s: Óscar Romero was Archbishop of San Salvador from 1977 to 1980. Initially considered a conservative, he became an outspoken critic of military repression and death squads, using his radio sermons to denounce killings.

oberto-doria.s: Oberto Doria was a Genoese admiral and statesman of the thirteenth century. From 1270 he shared power with Oberto Spinola as Captain of the People, a joint rule by the two great Ghibelline families that kept the Guelph nobles out of office.

oberto-spinola.s: Oberto Spinola was a Genoese nobleman of the thirteenth century and leader of the Ghibelline Spinola family who, with Oberto Doria, took power in Genoa in 1270 and governed as joint Captain of the People. Their dual rule excluded the Guelph families from office and coincided…

otto-perez-molina.s: Otto Pérez Molina (born 1950) is a retired Guatemalan general who was president from 2012 to 2015. A former head of military intelligence and a signatory of the 1996 peace accords, he was elected on promises of firm action against crime.

oswaldo-lopez-arellano.s: Oswaldo López Arellano (1921–2010) was a Honduran air force officer who seized power in a coup in October 1963 against President Ramón Villeda Morales and dominated Honduran politics until 1975. He ruled from 1963 to 1971, a period that included the Football War with El…

organization-of-american-states.s: The Organization of American States (OAS) is a regional organisation of the states of the Americas, founded in Bogotá in 1948 and based in Washington, DC. It promotes democracy, human rights, security and development, and it arranged the ceasefire in the Football War between…

organisation-armee-secrete.s: The Organisation armée secrète (OAS) was a clandestine French far-right paramilitary group formed in early 1961 by army officers and European settlers opposed to Algerian independence. Through bombings and assassinations in Algeria and France it tried to wreck the negotiations…

operation-blue-star.s: Operation Blue Star was the Indian Army's assault in June 1984 on the Golden Temple complex at Amritsar, the holiest shrine of Sikhism, to remove the armed Sikh militant leader Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale and his followers. The fighting killed Bhindranwale and hundreds of…

oncenio.s: The Oncenio (Eleven Years) is the name for the second government of Augusto B. Leguía in Peru, from his coup of July 1919 to his overthrow in August 1930. Under the slogan of a New Fatherland, Leguía centralised power, persecuted opponents and financed roads, ports and the…

onofrio-della-cava.s: Onofrio della Cava was a Neapolitan architect and engineer who built Dubrovnik's public water supply, completed in 1438, which brought water nearly 12 kilometres from a spring at Šumet. Its outlets in the city include the Large and Small Onofrio Fountains, which still stand.

orso-ipato.s: Orso Ipato was the third Doge of Venice in tradition but the first whose existence is securely attested, elected in 726 by the lagoon communities during the Iconoclast disputes. He helped the Byzantines recover Ravenna from the Lombards and received the honorary title of…

olaf-guild.s: The Olaf Guild, named after the Norwegian saint Olaf, was the oldest of the guilds of Reval (Tallinn). Its members were craftsmen of lower-status trades and, unusually, included Estonians as well as Germans, though Germans increasingly dominated it.

oxyrhynchus.s: Oxyrhynchus, modern el-Bahnasa, was a city of Middle Egypt west of the Nile and the capital of a nome in Ptolemaic and Roman times. Excavations by Bernard Grenfell and Arthur Hunt from 1896 recovered hundreds of thousands of papyrus fragments from its rubbish mounds.

origen.s: Origen was a Christian theologian and scholar of Alexandria and one of the most productive writers of the early church. He taught in Alexandria and later at Caesarea in Palestine, compiled the Hexapla, a comparison of versions of the Old Testament, and wrote commentaries and…

omoro-soshi.s: The Omoro Sōshi is a collection of 1,554 old Ryukyuan songs and chants in 22 volumes, compiled by the royal court at Shuri between 1531 and 1623. The songs, many of them sacred, praise kings, priestesses, voyages and places.

oyake-akahachi.s: Oyake Akahachi was a chieftain on Ishigaki Island in the Yaeyama Islands who led resistance to the Ryukyu Kingdom at the end of the fifteenth century. He refused tribute and rejected Shuri's interference in local religion, and in 1500 King Shō Shin sent a large fleet that…

othello.s: Othello is a tragedy by William Shakespeare, written around 1603 and first published in 1622. It tells of a Moorish general in the service of Venice who is driven by his scheming ensign Iago to murder his wife, Desdemona.

oroetes.s: Oroetes was the Persian satrap of Sardis under Cyrus the Great and Cambyses II. Around 522 BCE, according to Herodotus, he lured Polycrates of Samos to the mainland with a promise of treasure and had him killed.

otanes.s: Otanes was a Persian noble who, according to Herodotus, uncovered the false Smerdis and joined the conspiracy of seven that placed Darius I on the throne in 522 BCE; in the famous constitutional debate he argued for rule by the people. Around 517 BCE he led the Persian…

obotrites.s: The Obotrites were a confederation of West Slavic tribes in present-day Mecklenburg and eastern Holstein from the eighth to the twelfth centuries. Allies of Charlemagne against the Saxons, they received Nordalbingia after its people were deported in 804.

ogaden-war.s: The Ogaden War was fought between Somalia and Ethiopia in 1977–1978 over the Ogaden, the Somali-inhabited region of eastern Ethiopia. Somali forces invaded in July 1977 and overran most of the region, but the Soviet Union switched its support to Ethiopia's Derg regime, and…

ogpu.s: The OGPU (Joint State Political Directorate) was the Soviet political police from 1923 to 1934, successor to the Cheka and GPU. Led by Felix Dzerzhinsky and then Vyacheslav Menzhinsky, it suppressed opposition, staged early show trials and enforced the collectivisation of…

operation-barbarossa.s: Operation Barbarossa was the German invasion of the Soviet Union, launched on 22 June 1941 by some three million German troops with Romanian, Finnish and other allied forces. It destroyed much of the Red Army in huge encirclements at Białystok–Minsk, Smolensk and Kyiv and…

oau-liberation-committee.s: The OAU Liberation Committee was the body set up by the Organisation of African Unity at its founding in 1963 to coordinate and fund the liberation movements fighting colonial and white-minority rule in Africa. Based in Dar es Salaam, it supported movements in Mozambique,…

otumba.s: Otumba is a town in the State of Mexico, north-east of Mexico City, close to the ruins of Teotihuacan. Nearby obsidian sources were worked by the Teotihuacanos and later by the Aztecs, for whom Otumba was a craft centre.

osung.s: Ösung was a son of the Tibetan emperor Langdarma whose claim to the throne, disputed by his rival Yumten after Langdarma's death around 842, divided the court and contributed to the collapse of the Tibetan Empire. Through his son Pelkhortsen and grandson Kyide Nyimagon, his…

on-the-origin-of-species.s: On the Origin of Species is the book by Charles Darwin, published in London in November 1859, that set out the theory of evolution by natural selection. Arguing from extensive evidence that species descend with modification from common ancestors, it transformed biology and…

ophir.s: Ophir is a land famous for its gold in the Hebrew Bible, reached by the ships of Solomon and Hiram of Tyre sailing from Ezion-Geber on the Red Sea. Its location is unknown: scholars have proposed south-western Arabia, the Horn of Africa and the coasts of India, and an ostracon…

opec.n: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
opec.s: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is an intergovernmental organisation of oil-producing states founded at Baghdad in September 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela. It coordinates its members' petroleum policies, chiefly through…

orinoco-belt.s: The Orinoco Belt is a territory along the southern part of the eastern Orinoco River basin in Venezuela, about 600 km long, that holds one of the largest deposits of heavy and extra-heavy crude oil in the world. Its reserves make up most of Venezuela's proven reserves, the…

our-lady-of-vladimir.s: Our Lady of Vladimir is a Byzantine icon of the Virgin and Child, painted in Constantinople in the early twelfth century and sent to Kiev around 1130. Andrei Bogolyubsky took it to Vladimir in 1155, and in 1395 it was brought to Moscow, where it was credited with saving the…

oshel.s: Oshel was a fortified town of Volga Bulgaria on the Volga, named in the Russian chronicles. In 1220 an army of Vladimir-Suzdal sent by Grand Prince Yuri II stormed and burned it in reprisal for the Bulgars' capture of Ustyug, in one of the last major Russian campaigns against…

ouaddai-region.s: Ouaddaï is a province of eastern Chad on the border with Sudan, with its capital at Abéché. It takes its name from the Wadai Sultanate, whose heartland it covers, and is home to the Maba and other peoples.

odenwald.s: The Odenwald is a wooded upland region in southern Hesse, northern Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria, Germany, between the Rhine plain, the Main and the Neckar. In the Middle Ages and early modern period it was divided among the Electoral Palatinate, the Counts of Erbach, the…

odaenathus.s: Odaenathus was a ruler of Palmyra in Roman Syria and husband of Zenobia. After the Persian king Shapur I captured the emperor Valerian in 260, he attacked the retreating Persian army, suppressed the usurpers Macrianus and Quietus, and raided Sasanian territory as far as…

onomarchus.s: Onomarchus was the general of the Phocians in the Third Sacred War, succeeding Philomelus in 354 BCE. He used the treasures of Delphi to hire mercenaries, and in 353 BCE he twice defeated Philip II of Macedon in Thessaly.

of-plymouth-plantation.s: Of Plymouth Plantation is a history of the Pilgrims and Plymouth Colony written by William Bradford, the colony's long-serving governor, between 1630 and 1651. It covers the Separatists' years in Leiden, the Mayflower voyage and the colony's first decades.

oecusse.s: Oecusse is an exclave of East Timor on the north coast of the western, Indonesian half of Timor. Around Lifau it was the earliest centre of Portuguese presence on the island, and the border treaties with the Netherlands of 1859 and 1914 left it as a Portuguese enclave within…

ohrigstad.s: Ohrigstad, originally Andries-Ohrigstad, is a small town in Mpumalanga, South Africa. Voortrekkers under Andries Hendrik Potgieter founded it in 1845 as the capital of a Boer settlement beyond British reach, naming it after Potgieter and the Dutch merchant Georgius Ohrig.

opechancanough.s: Opechancanough was paramount chief of the Powhatan Confederacy in Virginia and a younger brother of Wahunsenacah. He led the surprise attacks of 1622 and 1644 that killed hundreds of English colonists in an attempt to drive them out.

oker.s: The Oker is a river in Lower Saxony, Germany, flowing about 125 kilometres north from the Harz past Wolfenbüttel and Brunswick to join the Aller. Brunswick, the chief town of the Guelph dukes, grew up on its banks, and the lands of the bishops of Hildesheim lay to its west.

ortenau.s: The Ortenau is a region of Baden in south-western Germany, lying between the Rhine and the western slopes of the Black Forest, with Offenburg as its main town. In the Middle Ages it was divided among the bishops of Strasbourg, local lords and small imperial cities, while the…

old-prussians.s: The Old Prussians were a Baltic people who lived between the lower Vistula and the Neman on the south-eastern coast of the Baltic Sea. Pagan into the 13th century, they were conquered by the Teutonic Order between the 1230s and the 1280s after fierce resistance, and German and…

obersalzberg.s: The Obersalzberg is a mountainside above Berchtesgaden in the Bavarian Alps. From the 1920s Adolf Hitler stayed there, and after 1933 the area was turned into a fenced compound with his Berghof, houses for Nazi leaders, barracks and the Kehlsteinhaus on the summit above.

otto-i-duke-of-brunswick-gottingen.s: Otto I, known as Otto the Bad, was Duke of Brunswick-Göttingen from 1367 to 1394. He spent his reign in feuds with neighbouring princes, knights and towns, above all his own town of Göttingen, whose citizens stormed the ducal castle in the town in 1387 and defeated his forces.

osterode-am-harz.s: Osterode am Harz is a town on the western edge of the Harz in Lower Saxony, Germany. First recorded in the 12th century, it belonged to the Guelph Principality of Grubenhagen and later to Hanover, and grew as a market and trading town serving the Harz silver mines.

ozurgeti.s: Ozurgeti is a town in western Georgia, the administrative centre of the Guria region, a short distance inland from the Black Sea coast. It served as the residence of the Gurieli princes of Guria and, after the Russian annexation of 1829, as the seat of a district.

offenbach-am-main.s: Offenbach am Main is a city in Hesse, Germany, on the Main opposite Frankfurt. It belonged to the counts, later princes, of Isenburg, who welcomed Huguenot refugees at the end of the 17th century, and it grew into an industrial town known above all for leather goods.

oranienstein-palace.s: Oranienstein Palace is a baroque palace above the Lahn at Diez in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, built from 1672 to 1684 on the site of a former convent for Albertine Agnes of Nassau, widow of Count William Frederick of Nassau-Diez. It was the German residence of the…

odoyev.s: Odoyev is a small town in Tula Oblast, Russia, on the Upa river. In the 14th and 15th centuries it was the seat of the princes of Novosil, who took the name Odoyevsky from it, and it passed between Lithuanian and Muscovite overlordship before the Upper Oka princes went over to…

obrenovic-dynasty.s: The Obrenović dynasty ruled Serbia from 1815 to 1842 and again from 1858 to 1903. Founded by Miloš Obrenović, leader of the Second Serbian Uprising, it competed for the throne with the Karađorđević family.

order-of-the-sun-of-peru.n: Order of the Sun of Peru
order-of-the-sun-of-peru.s: The Order of the Sun of Peru is the country's highest state decoration, founded by José de San Martín on 8 October 1821 to reward those who served the cause of independence. Abolished in 1825, it was restored in 1921, and it is regarded as the oldest civil and military order…

osiris.s: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian god of the dead, the afterlife and regeneration, shown as a mummified king. In myth he was murdered by his brother Seth and revived by his wife Isis, becoming the father of Horus and ruler of the underworld.

oregon-city-oregon.s: Oregon City is a city on the Willamette River beside Willamette Falls in Oregon, United States, laid out in the early 1840s by John McLoughlin of the Hudson's Bay Company. It was the seat of the provisional government and the first capital of Oregon Territory, and the official…

oregon-country.s: The Oregon Country was the region of north-western North America west of the Rocky Mountains between California and Russian America. Britain and the United States agreed in 1818 to occupy it jointly, while the Hudson's Bay Company dominated its fur trade.

oregon-territory.s: Oregon Territory was an organised territory of the United States from 1848 to 1859, covering the present states of Oregon, Washington and Idaho and parts of Montana and Wyoming. Created by Congress after the Oregon Treaty and the Whitman massacre, it replaced the settlers'…

oregon-trail.s: The Oregon Trail was an overland wagon route of about 3,500 km from Independence, Missouri, to the Willamette Valley in Oregon. From the early 1840s to the 1860s hundreds of thousands of emigrants used it and its branches to Oregon and California, travelling for four to six…

organic-laws-of-oregon.s: The Organic Laws of Oregon were the legal codes adopted by the Provisional Government of Oregon, first in July 1843 and revised in 1845. Based partly on the statutes of Iowa, they set up an executive, legislature and courts, banned slavery and allowed settlers to claim up to…

operation-bootstrap.s: Operation Bootstrap was the programme launched in Puerto Rico in the late 1940s by Luis Muñoz Marín and Teodoro Moscoso to industrialise the island's farming economy. It attracted US manufacturers with tax exemptions and cheap labour, turning Puerto Rico into a manufacturing…

orongo.s: Orongo is a ceremonial village on the rim of the Rano Kau crater at the south-western tip of Rapa Nui (Easter Island). Its low stone houses and rock carvings of bird men were the centre of the Tangata manu cult, in which competitors swam to the islet of Motu Nui to bring back…

oslofjord.s: The Oslofjord is an inlet of the Skagerrak in south-eastern Norway, stretching about 100 kilometres north to Oslo. Its western shore held the Viking Age centres of Vestfold, with the ship burials of Oseberg and Gokstad, and its eastern side the district of Vingulmark.

operation-sheepskin.s: Operation Sheepskin was the British landing on Anguilla on 19 March 1969 to end the island's self-declared break from the associated state of Saint Kitts-Nevis-Anguilla. Some 300 paratroopers and a contingent of London Metropolitan Police officers arrived unopposed, and the…

ordubad.s: Ordubad is a town in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic of Azerbaijan, on the Aras River near the borders with Iran and Armenia. An old centre of silk production and trade, it keeps a well-preserved historic quarter.

oyapock-river.s: The Oyapock is a river of northern South America that forms most of the border between French Guiana and the Brazilian state of Amapá, flowing about 400 km to the Atlantic. France claimed land as far south as the Araguari, but Swiss arbitration in 1900 fixed the boundary on…

ophellas.s: Ophellas was a Macedonian officer of Alexander the Great who conquered Cyrene for Ptolemy I in 322 BCE and governed it. He later made himself independent, and in 308 BCE he led an army west to join Agathocles of Syracuse in his war against Carthage.

orasac.s: Orašac is a village in the Šumadija region of central Serbia, near Aranđelovac. In February 1804 Serbian notables met there and chose Karađorđe Petrović to lead a revolt against the dahijas, the renegade janissary rulers of the Belgrade pashalik, beginning the First Serbian…

ombrone.s: The Ombrone is a river of southern Tuscany, Italy, which rises in the hills near Siena and flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea south of Grosseto. Its lower plain was once largely occupied by the lagoon of Lake Prile, beside which the Etruscan city of Rusellae stood.

omsk.s: Omsk is a city in south-western Siberia, Russia, at the confluence of the Irtysh and Om rivers. Founded as a fortress in 1716, it became the administrative centre of the Steppe region.

osco-umbrian-languages.s: The Osco-Umbrian languages, also called Sabellic, are a group of extinct Italic languages once spoken across central and southern Italy. The best known are Oscan, used by the Samnites and their neighbours, and Umbrian, preserved in the Iguvine Tablets.

owari-province.s: Owari Province was an old province of central Japan, corresponding to the western part of modern Aichi Prefecture around Nagoya. It was the home of Oda Nobunaga, who united it by 1559, and of Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

osaka.s: Osaka is one of the largest cities of Japan and the centre of the Kansai region, at the mouth of the Yodo river on Osaka Bay. Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle there from 1583 on the site of the Ishiyama Hongan-ji temple-fortress, and after the Tokugawa destroyed the…

osaka-bay.s: Osaka Bay is an arm of the Seto Inland Sea on the coast of the Kansai region of Japan, bounded by Awaji Island to the west. The ports on its shores, among them Sakai, Hyogo (Kobe) and Osaka, were for centuries the gateways of the Kyoto region to western Japan, China and the…

ohkay-owingeh.s: Ohkay Owingeh, formerly San Juan Pueblo, is a Tewa pueblo on the Rio Grande north of Santa Fe, New Mexico. In 1598 Juan de Oñate made it the first headquarters of the Spanish colony of New Mexico, naming it San Juan de los Caballeros.

okubo-toshimichi.s: Okubo Toshimichi was a samurai of the Satsuma Domain and one of the leading statesmen of the Meiji Restoration of 1868. With Saigo Takamori and Kido Takayoshi he engineered the alliance of Satsuma and Choshu and the overthrow of the Tokugawa shogunate, then directed the new…

old-saybrook.s: Old Saybrook is a town in Connecticut, United States, at the mouth of the Connecticut River on Long Island Sound. It grew from Saybrook Fort, built in 1635–1636 under John Winthrop the Younger for the Puritan holders of the Warwick Patent and named after Lord Saye and Sele and…

osceola.s: Osceola was a Seminole war leader who led resistance to removal from Florida in the Second Seminole War. In 1837 he was seized by American troops while meeting them under a flag of truce, an act widely condemned.

orthagorids.s: The Orthagorids were the dynasty of tyrants who ruled Sicyon in the north-eastern Peloponnese for about a century, from around 665 to the mid-6th century BCE. Aristotle called their rule the longest-lasting tyranny in Greece, explaining it by their moderation.

oise.s: The Oise is a river of Belgium and northern France, rising in the Belgian Ardennes and flowing south-west for about 340 kilometres to join the Seine near Paris at Conflans-Sainte-Honorine. Its valley, with towns such as Compiègne and Pontoise, has long been a route between…

oise-department.s: Oise is a department of northern France in the Hauts-de-France region, created in 1790 and named after the river Oise. Its prefecture is Beauvais, and it includes Compiègne, Senlis and Chantilly.

oranjestad-sint-eustatius.s: Oranjestad is the capital and only town of Sint Eustatius, a Dutch island in the Caribbean. Its harbour below Fort Oranje, built by the Dutch from 1636, made it in the 18th century one of the busiest free ports of the Caribbean, nicknamed the Golden Rock, where traders…

okhtyrka.s: Okhtyrka is a city in Sumy Oblast in north-eastern Ukraine, on the Vorskla river. Founded around 1641 as a Polish frontier fortress and soon settled by Cossacks under Muscovite rule, it was the seat of one of the five Cossack regiments of Sloboda Ukraine until 1765.

ostrogozhsk.s: Ostrogozhsk is a town in Voronezh Oblast in Russia, on the Tikhaya Sosna river near its junction with the Don. It was founded in 1652 by Ukrainian Cossacks led by Ivan Dzinkovsky, who had moved into Muscovite territory, and became the seat of the Ostrogozhsk Cossack regiment…

old-smyrna.s: Old Smyrna is the archaeological site of the first city of Smyrna, on the mound of Tepekule at Bayraklı on the north-eastern shore of the Gulf of Izmir, Turkey. Settled by Aeolian and then Ionian Greeks in the early Iron Age, it was a walled city with one of the earliest…

ordos-plateau.s: The Ordos Plateau is a high, partly desert region of northern China, enclosed on three sides by the great northern loop of the Yellow River and now mainly in Inner Mongolia. A frontier between Chinese farmers and steppe peoples, it was contested by the Xiongnu and the Han,…

odendaal-plan.s: The Odendaal Plan was a scheme for South West Africa (Namibia) proposed in 1964 by a South African commission under Frans Hendrik Odendaal. It applied apartheid's homeland policy to the territory, dividing it into ethnic homelands for the black population and a larger area for…

oeiras-piaui.s: Oeiras is a town in the Brazilian state of Piauí that grew from a cattle-ranching settlement and became the first capital of the captaincy of Piauí in the eighteenth century, named after the Portuguese title of the Marquis of Pombal, Count of Oeiras. It remained the capital…

orbetello.s: Orbetello is a town in southern Tuscany, built on a narrow spit in the middle of a lagoon between the mainland and Monte Argentario. From 1557 it was the capital of the Spanish State of the Presidi, which ringed it with powerful fortifications, and it was joined to Tuscany in…

osman-yusuf-kenadid.s: Osman Yusuf Kenadid was a Somali poet and scholar, a son of Sultan Yusuf Ali Kenadid of Hobyo. Around 1920 he devised the Osmanya script, the first widely used indigenous alphabet for the Somali language.

osmanya.s: Osmanya is an alphabet for the Somali language created around 1920 by Osman Yusuf Kenadid, son of the sultan of Hobyo. Written from left to right, its letters drew partly on Arabic and Ethiopic forms.

oued-righ.s: The Oued Righ is a valley of oases in the north-eastern Algerian Sahara, stretching for about 150 kilometres north of Touggourt. Its date palm groves were watered by artesian wells dug by specialist well-divers.

ortygia.s: Ortygia is a small island forming the historic centre of Syracuse in Sicily, joined to the mainland by bridges. Corinthian colonists settled it in 734 or 733 BCE, drawn by its two harbours and the freshwater spring of Arethusa.

odiel.s: The Odiel is a river of Huelva province in south-western Spain, rising in the Sierra de Aracena and flowing south to the Atlantic. At Huelva it meets the Río Tinto in a shared estuary, whose marshes, the Marismas del Odiel, are a protected wetland.

orestes-mythology.s: Orestes was a hero of Greek myth, the son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, who avenged his father's murder by killing his mother and her lover Aegisthus. His story is the subject of Aeschylus's Oresteia and of plays by Sophocles and Euripides.

orestes-roman-general.s: Orestes was a Roman politician and general of the late Western Empire, who had once served as a secretary of Attila the Hun. As master of soldiers he drove out the emperor Julius Nepos in 475 and made his young son Romulus Augustulus emperor.

oaxaca.s: Oaxaca is a state of southern Mexico on the Pacific coast, with its capital at Oaxaca de Juárez. Its mountains and valleys were home to the Zapotec and Mixtec civilisations, including the city of Monte Albán, and the region was conquered by the Aztecs in the 15th century and…
