orinoco.s: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers of South America, flowing about 2,140 kilometres from the Guiana Highlands through Venezuela and along the Colombian border to a vast delta on the Atlantic. Its plains, the llanos, were a battleground of the independence wars, and its…

omurtag.s: Omurtag was khan of the First Bulgarian Empire from 814 to 831. He concluded a thirty-year peace with Byzantium around 815, fixing the border in Thrace, fought the Franks over the middle Danube in the 820s, and built palaces and fortifications at Pliska and on the Danube.

ocotelolco.s: Ocotelolco was one of the four altepetl, or city-states, that together formed the Nahua state of Tlaxcala in central Mexico, alongside Tepeticpac, Quiahuixtlan and Tizatlan. By the early 16th century it was the richest and most powerful of the four, with the main market, and…

okazaki.s: Okazaki is a city in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, in the former province of Mikawa. Its castle was the seat of the Matsudaira family, and Tokugawa Ieyasu was born there in 1543; after the death of Imagawa Yoshimoto in 1560 he returned to Okazaki and made it the base of his…

ovid.s: Ovid was a Roman poet, born at Sulmo in the land of the Paeligni in 43 BCE, the author of the Metamorphoses, the Art of Love and the Fasti, a poem on the Roman calendar and its festivals. In 8 CE Augustus banished him to Tomis on the Black Sea, where he wrote the Tristia and…

oromo-liberation-front.s: The Oromo Liberation Front is a political organisation founded in 1973 to pursue self-determination for the Oromo people of Ethiopia. It joined the Transitional Government formed after the fall of the Derg in 1991 but withdrew in 1992, accusing the EPRDF of persecution, and…

olmecs.s: The Olmecs were the earliest major civilisation of Mesoamerica, flourishing in the Gulf Coast lowlands of southern Veracruz and Tabasco in Mexico from about 1200 to 400 BCE. Their centres, San Lorenzo, La Venta and Tres Zapotes, are known for colossal stone heads, jade…

orihuela.s: Orihuela is a city in the province of Alicante in eastern Spain, on the Segura river. It is the first of the seven towns named in the treaty of 713 between Theodemir and the Muslim conquerors, and it may have been his seat, giving the region of Tudmir its centre.

osorkon-the-elder.s: Osorkon the Elder was a king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt in the late 10th century BCE, ruling from Tanis for about six years. He was the first pharaoh of Libyan descent, a member of the Meshwesh chiefly family settled at Bubastis and an uncle of Shoshenq I.

osorkon-i.s: Osorkon I was the second king of the Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt, son of Shoshenq I, reigning for about 35 years in the late 10th and early 9th centuries BCE. He made lavish gifts to temples across Egypt, recorded at Bubastis.

otepaa.s: Otepää is a town in southern Estonia, built beside a hillfort that was the main stronghold of the ancient Estonian county of Ugandi; its name means 'bear's head'. During the Livonian Crusade of the early 13th century the fort changed hands several times between the Estonians,…

odonovan-family.s: The O'Donovans, in Irish Ó Donnabháin, are an Irish family descended from Donnubán mac Cathail, a 10th-century king of the Uí Fidgenti in County Limerick. Displaced by Anglo-Norman settlers around the early 13th century, they moved south into Carbery in west Cork.

okinawa-reversion-agreement.s: The Okinawa Reversion Agreement was a treaty between the United States and Japan, signed on 17 June 1971, under which the Ryukyu Islands, administered by the United States since 1945, returned to Japanese sovereignty on 15 May 1972. The United States kept its military bases on…

organic-acts-of-the-virgin-islands.n: Organic Acts of the Virgin Islands
organic-acts-of-the-virgin-islands.s: The Organic Acts of the Virgin Islands are laws of the United States Congress that serve as the territory's constitution. The first, of 1936, created elected municipal councils for St Croix and for St Thomas and St John and extended voting rights; the Revised Organic Act of…

oral-kazakhstan.s: Oral, known in Russian as Uralsk, is a city in north-western Kazakhstan on the Ural River. Founded in the early 17th century as Yaitsky Gorodok, the chief settlement of the Yaik Cossacks, it was a centre of Yemelyan Pugachev's rebellion in 1773–1774, after which Catherine the…

omura-masujiro.s: Ōmura Masujirō, born Murata Zōroku, was a Japanese physician and scholar of Western learning who became the founder of Japan's modern army. He served the Uwajima domain, where he helped build a steamship, and later the Chōshū domain, whose forces he reorganised and led to…

ordu-baliq.s: Ordu-Baliq was the capital of the Uyghur Khaganate on the Orkhon River in central Mongolia, built in the mid-8th century under Bayanchur Khan. Its ruins, known as Karabalgasun, include massive walls, a citadel and a palace, and travellers described a walled city surrounded by…

olof-tratalja.s: Olof Trätälja, 'the Tree-Feller', is a legendary Swedish king of the Yngling line known from Ynglingatal and Snorri Sturluson's Ynglinga saga. Driven from Uppsala, he is said to have cleared the forests of Värmland and founded a settlement there, before being sacrificed to…

oseberg-ship.s: The Oseberg ship is a richly carved Viking ship found in a burial mound at Oseberg near Tønsberg in Vestfold, Norway, and excavated in 1904. Its timbers were felled in 820, and the burial took place in 834.

ostfold.s: Østfold is a region of south-eastern Norway on the eastern side of the Oslofjord, bordering Sweden, with towns such as Fredrikstad, Sarpsborg, Moss and Halden. In the Viking Age it formed the core of the petty kingdom of Vingulmark, and it was long a frontier exposed to Danish…

orthez.s: Orthez is a town on the Gave de Pau in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department of south-western France. It became the capital of Béarn under the viscounts of the Moncade line in the 13th century, and Gaston Fébus held his court in its Moncade castle in the 14th.

olt-river.s: The Olt is a river of Romania, about 615 km long, that rises in the Eastern Carpathians, flows through south-eastern Transylvania, cuts through the Southern Carpathians by the Red Tower Pass and runs south to the Danube. It divides Wallachia into Oltenia, named after it, to…

ode-itsekiri.s: Ode-Itsekiri, known to European traders as Big Warri, is a town on an island in the creeks of the western Niger Delta, in today's Delta State of Nigeria. It was the traditional capital of the Itsekiri kingdom of Warri, founded around 1480 according to tradition, and the seat…

olu-of-warri.s: The Olu of Warri is the title of the king of the Itsekiri people of the western Niger Delta in Nigeria. The line traces its origin to Ginuwa, a Benin prince of the late 15th century, and its traditional seat is Ode-Itsekiri.

orda-khan.s: Orda was the eldest son of Jochi and a grandson of Genghis Khan. In the division of the Jochid lands he received the eastern part, the left wing of the ulus east of the Ural River, later known as the White Horde or, in some sources, the Blue Horde.

oroonoko.s: Oroonoko, or The Royal Slave, is a short novel by Aphra Behn published in 1688. It tells of an African prince who is tricked into slavery and taken to the English colony of Suriname, where he leads a revolt of enslaved people and is executed.

omer-bodson.s: Omer Bodson (1856–1891) was a Belgian officer in the service of the Congo Free State and a member of the Stairs Expedition to Katanga. At Bunkeya on 20 December 1891 he shot dead the Yeke king Msiri during a confrontation and was himself mortally wounded by Msiri's men.

ottoman-hungarian-wars.s: The Ottoman–Hungarian wars were the conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the Kingdom of Hungary from the late 14th century to 1526. Hungary led crusades against the Ottomans that ended in defeat at Nicopolis (1396) and Varna (1444), while John Hunyadi relieved Belgrade in…

ottoman-safavid-war-1623-1639.s: The Ottoman–Safavid War of 1623–1639 was the last major war between the Ottoman Empire and Safavid Iran. It began when Shah Abbas I took Baghdad in 1624; the Ottomans failed for years to retake it, until Sultan Murad IV recaptured the city in 1638.

ottoman-persian-wars.s: The Ottoman–Persian Wars were the conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the successive dynasties of Iran, from the Safavids to the Qajars, between 1514 and 1823. Fought over eastern Anatolia, the Caucasus and Mesopotamia, they began with the Ottoman victory at Chaldiran and…

ottoman-safavid-war-1532-1555.s: The Ottoman–Safavid War of 1532–1555 was fought between the Ottoman Empire of Suleiman the Magnificent and Safavid Persia under Tahmasp I. Suleiman led three campaigns into Persia and took Baghdad and much of Mesopotamia in 1534; the Peace of Amasya (1555), the first formal…

ottoman-venetian-war-1570-1573.s: The Ottoman–Venetian War of 1570–1573 was fought between the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Venice, allied with Spain and the papacy in the Holy League. The Ottomans conquered Cyprus, taking Nicosia in 1570 and Famagusta in 1571; the Holy League destroyed the Ottoman fleet…

olmec-colossal-heads.s: The Olmec colossal heads are seventeen heads carved from basalt boulders by the Olmec civilisation of Mexico's Gulf Coast: ten from San Lorenzo, four from La Venta, two from Tres Zapotes and one from La Cobata. Up to 3.4 metres high, each wears a distinctive headdress, and…

olaudah-equiano.s: Olaudah Equiano, known for most of his life as Gustavus Vassa, was a writer and abolitionist in Britain. By his own account he was kidnapped as a child from an Igbo village in what is now Nigeria, though the historian Vincent Carretta, citing a baptism record that places his…

oliver-tambo.s: Oliver Tambo was a South African anti-apartheid politician and activist who led the African National Congress from 1967 to 1991. With Nelson Mandela and Walter Sisulu he helped found the ANC Youth League in 1944, and became the ANC's secretary-general in 1955.

olympe-de-gouges.s: Olympe de Gouges was a French playwright and political activist, best known for her Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen. Writing plays in Paris from the 1780s, she was also one of France's earliest public opponents of slavery.
